title: Introduce GPU region sampler and cumulative epoch counters for scheduling microbenchmarks
author: Maya Thompson
description: Context: We need low-overhead, deployment-friendly instrumentation to profile GPU hot paths (kernel launch/sync, cross-stream scheduling and KV cache hits) across continuous-batching workloads so schedulers and kernel-selection heuristics can be tuned with real microbench data. This PR adds a lightweight GPU region sampler, cumulative epoch counters, and a tiny harness to export aggregated microbench results to the perf dashboard. Motivation: existing profilers (full CUPTI traces, perfetto) are heavy in continuous-batching repros and produce too much data for CI-regression runs. The goal is a middle ground: O(1-2%) overhead in production with aggregated, roll-up counters useful for trend dashboards and fast regression tests. Summary of changes: 1) runtime/profiler/region_sampler.cpp/h: a low-overhead sampler that annotates start/end GPU regions with a compact 64-bit tag and records per-region wall/NVTX-adjacent timestamps when enabled. The sampler is lock-minimal and uses per-thread ring buffers with a single atomic head pointer to avoid contended mutexes under high concurrency. 2) runtime/profiler/epoch_counters.h/cpp: cumulative epoch counters (numeric and histogram buckets) that aggregate metrics per logical epoch (configurable period tied to batch count or time window). Counters include kernel_launch_count, avg_kernel_latency_ns, kvcache_hit_rate_p1000, batch_size_hist_buckets. 3) tools/mini-prof/bench_driver.cc: a small binary to run microbench loops, push continuous-batching scenarios, and emit summary JSON compatible with our perf dashboard ingest. 4) observability/exports/region-sampler-dashboard.json: dashboard panels for epoch counters and trends, plus a short README at docs/observability/microprof.md showing how to enable and interpret metrics. 5) runtime/config: adds --enable-microprof flag and sampling_rate parameter (default disabled in production). Commits (high level): - Add region sampler and per-thread ring buffer (author: Maya) - Add epoch counters and Prometheus exporter glue (author: Maya) - Add mini-prof harness and dashboard export (author: Maya) - Tests: unit tests for counter overflow and stress microbench (author: Maya) - Fix: replace mutex with atomic head pointer to reduce contention (author: Maya) Files changed (high-level paths): runtime/profiler/region_sampler.cpp runtime/profiler/region_sampler.h runtime/profiler/epoch_counters.cpp runtime/profiler/epoch_counters.h tools/mini-prof/bench_driver.cc docs/observability/microprof.md observability/exports/region-sampler-dashboard.json Compatibility/feature flags: instrumentation is gated behind --enable-microprof and sampling_rate; all counters are optional exports and default to off for hosted customers. Metrics exposure: counters are exposed to Prometheus (runtime/metrics namespace: runtime_microprof_epoch_*), and bench driver emits a condensed JSON that can be uploaded to the perf dashboard or attached to PRs. Performance: microbench regression harness reports ~1.7% median overhead on p4d-like instance with continuous batching (95th percentile < 3.1%). We intentionally keep payload small (compact tags, integer counters) to enable long-running collection. Review conversation (high level): - Alex Rivera: "Looks good overall; can we avoid a global mutex in hotpath?" Author: "Agreed, switched to per-thread ring buffers with atomic head/tail; updated tests to stress 128 threads." - Priya Nair: "We need clear semantics for epoch boundaries in autoscaling scenarios." Author: "Added epoch boundary config (time/window) and documented behavior in microprof.md; added unit tests covering boundary alignment across restarts." - Luca Bianchi: "Prometheus cardinality concerns — bucketize batch sizes and sample kvcache hits scaled by 1000 to send ints only." Author: "Implemented fixed-size histogram buckets and scaled counters; noted export caveats in docs." CI and validation: - Unit tests: pass - Integration microbench: pass on linux/amd64 and linux/aarch64 runners - Flaky test: runtime/test_scheduler::ConcurrencyStress was fixed by the atomic ring change - Perf regression: baseline vs this branch shows acceptable overhead; artifacts uploaded to CI build number 8421 (artifact: mini-prof-summary-8421.json) Merge notes: PR merged via squash after final approval from Priya and CI green on rerun. Merged commit message summarizes the feature and points to ENG-1427/ENG-1503 for follow-ups. Release notes: "Add experimental lightweight GPU region sampler and epoch counters for microbenching and perf dashboards; opt-in via --enable-microprof. Use mini-prof harness to collect summarized traces for scheduling and KV cache tuning. (experimental, default off)" How to test locally: 1) build //tools/mini-prof: bazel build //tools/mini-prof:bench_driver 2) enable on runtime: --enable-microprof --sampling_rate=1000 3) run bench_driver against local runtime and upload JSON to dashboard ingest endpoint (see docs/observability/microprof.md) Follow-ups and TODOs: - Add optional speedscope timeline exporter in a follow-up to keep CI artifacts small - Hook the epoch counters into the autoscaler telemetry pipeline (ENG-1503) - Add safe KMS-safe export path for private deployments (security review ticket assigned) Notes on uniqueness: this PR focuses on compact cumulative counters and per-thread ring sampler (atomic head pointer) rather than full-trace CUPTI/CUDA timelines; it targets CI-friendly, low-overhead collection for continuous-batching workloads.
release_notes: Add experimental lightweight GPU region sampler and epoch counters for microbenching and perf dashboards; opt-in via --enable-microprof. Use mini-prof harness to collect summarized traces for scheduling and KV cache tuning. (experimental, default off)
short_summary: Adds low-overhead GPU region sampler, epoch-aggregated counters, and a mini profiling harness to emit condensed microbench artifacts for perf dashboards and scheduling tuning. Gated behind --enable-microprof.
